claim: Human cytomegalovirus (HCMV) downregulates >900 human proteins during viral replication.
source: Human cytomegalovirus (HCMV) extensively modulates host cells, downregulating >900 human proteins during viral replication and degrading ≥133 proteins shortly after infection.
evidence: This claim is stated in the abstract and is supported by references to prior work by the authors (Nightingale et al., 2018; Weekes et al., 2014).

claim: HCMV degrades ≥133 proteins shortly after infection.
source: Human cytomegalovirus (HCMV) extensively modulates host cells, downregulating >900 human proteins during viral replication and degrading ≥133 proteins shortly after infection.
evidence: This claim is stated in the abstract and is supported by references to prior work (Nightingale et al., 2018; Weekes et al., 2014).

claim: A mass spectrometry-based interactome analysis of 169 tagged, stably-expressed canonical strain Merlin HCMV proteins was performed in infected cells.
source: We performed a mass spectrometry-based interactome analysis of 169 tagged, stably-expressed canonical strain Merlin HCMV proteins, and two non-canonical HCMV proteins, in infected cells.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: A mass spectrometry-based interactome analysis of two non-canonical HCMV proteins was performed in infected cells.
source: We performed a mass spectrometry-based interactome analysis of 169 tagged, stably-expressed canonical strain Merlin HCMV proteins, and two non-canonical HCMV proteins, in infected cells.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: The interactome analysis identified a network of >3400 virus-host protein interactions.
source: This identified a network of >3400 virus-host and >150 virus-virus protein interactions, providing insights into functions for multiple viral genes.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the interactome analysis.

claim: The interactome analysis identified a network of >150 virus-virus protein interactions.
source: This identified a network of >3400 virus-host and >150 virus-virus protein interactions, providing insights into functions for multiple viral genes.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results from the interactome analysis.

claim: Domain analysis predicted binding of the viral UL25 protein to SH3 domains of NCK Adaptor Protein-1.
source: Domain analysis predicted binding of the viral UL25 protein to SH3 domains of NCK Adaptor Protein-1.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental validation shown in Figure 4.

claim: Viral interacting proteins were identified for 31/133 degraded host targets.
source: Viral interacting proteins were identified for 31/133 degraded host targets.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Supplementary file 6.

claim: The uncharacterised, non-canonical ORFL147C protein interacts with elements of the mRNA splicing machinery.
source: Finally, the uncharacterised, non-canonical ORFL147C protein was found to interact with elements of the mRNA splicing machinery, and a mutational study suggested its importance in viral replication.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 6.

claim: A mutational study suggested the importance of ORFL147C in viral replication.
source: Finally, the uncharacterised, non-canonical ORFL147C protein was found to interact with elements of the mRNA splicing machinery, and a mutational study suggested its importance in viral replication.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by growth curve data in Figure 6F.

claim: HCMV persistently infects the majority of the worldwide population.
source: Human cytomegalovirus (HCMV) persistently infects the majority of the worldwide population (Mocarski et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a statement supported by a citation to established literature.

claim: Following primary infection under the control of a healthy immune system, a latent HCMV infection is established that persists lifelong.
source: Following primary infection under the control of a healthy immune system, a latent infection is established that persists lifelong (Reeves et al., 2005).
evidence: This is a statement supported by a citation to established literature.

claim: In immunocompromised individuals, particularly transplant recipients and AIDS patients, virus reactivated from latency to induce lytic infection is capable of affecting almost any organ system and causing serious disease.
source: In immunocompromised individuals, particularly transplant recipients and AIDS patients, virus reactivated from latency to induce lytic infection is capable of affecting almost any organ system and causing serious disease (Nichols et al., 2002).
evidence: This is a statement supported by a citation to established literature.

claim: HCMV infection in utero is a leading cause of deafness and intellectual disability in newborns, affecting ~1/200 pregnancies.
source: HCMV infection in utero is a leading cause of deafness and intellectual disability in newborns, affecting ~1/200 pregnancies (Mocarski et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a statement supported by a citation to established literature.

claim: Small-molecule disruption of critical virus-virus or virus-host protein interactions could provide novel therapeutic strategies.
source: Small-molecule disruption of critical virus-virus or virus-host protein interactions could provide novel therapeutic strategies.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential therapeutic applications.

claim: Disruption of interactions between antiviral restriction factors (ARFs) and viral antagonists can facilitate endogenous inhibition of infection.
source: Indeed, disruption of interactions between antiviral restriction factors (ARFs) and viral antagonists can facilitate endogenous inhibition of infection (Nathans et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a statement supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: HCMV encodes 170 canonical protein-coding genes.
source: HCMV encodes 170 canonical protein-coding genes (Gatherer et al., 2011), and a substantial number of non-canonical open reading frames (ORFs) that potentially encode additional proteins have been identified by ribosomal footprinting and proteomics (Nightingale et al., 2018; Stern-Ginossar et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a statement supported by a citation to established literature.

claim: A substantial number of non-canonical open reading frames (ORFs) that potentially encode additional HCMV proteins have been identified by ribosomal footprinting and proteomics.
source: HCMV encodes 170 canonical protein-coding genes (Gatherer et al., 2011), and a substantial number of non-canonical open reading frames (ORFs) that potentially encode additional proteins have been identified by ribosomal footprinting and proteomics (Nightingale et al., 2018; Stern-Ginossar et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations to prior work.

claim: During productive HCMV infection in vitro, gene expression is conventionally divided into immediate-early, early and late phases over a replication cycle lasting ~96 hr.
source: During productive infection in vitro, HCMV gene expression is conventionally divided into immediate-early, early and late phases over a replication cycle lasting ~96 hr.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about HCMV infection kinetics.

claim: Five temporal classes of viral protein expression have been defined by measuring viral protein profiles over time.
source: Five temporal classes of viral protein expression have been defined by measuring viral protein profiles over time (Weekes et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a statement supported by a citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: UL138 downregulates Multidrug Resistance-Associated Protein 1 (MRP1) during both productive infection and latency.
source: For example, UL138, which plays roles in the establishment and maintenance of latent infection, downregulates Multidrug Resistance-Associated Protein 1 (MRP1) during both phases of infection (Weekes et al., 2013; Weekes et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations to prior work by the authors.

claim: The functions of many canonical HCMV proteins remain poorly understood.
source: The functions of many canonical HCMV proteins remain poorly understood, and it is not yet clear how many, if any, non-canonical ORFs encode functional polypeptides.
evidence: This is a statement of the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: It is not yet clear how many, if any, non-canonical ORFs encode functional polypeptides.
source: The functions of many canonical HCMV proteins remain poorly understood, and it is not yet clear how many, if any, non-canonical ORFs encode functional polypeptides.
evidence: This is a statement of the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: 133 host proteins are degraded in the proteasome or lysosome during the early phase of HCMV infection.
source: We have shown previously that >900 host proteins are downregulated >3 fold over the course of HCMV infection, with 133 proteins degraded in the proteasome or lysosome during the early phase (Nightingale et al., 2018; Weekes et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations to prior work by the authors.

claim: It is not yet known which viral factors target most degraded host proteins.
source: However, it is not yet known which viral factors target these proteins, and certain proteins, including MHC class I molecules and natural killer cell ligands, can be targeted by more than one viral factor (Fielding et al., 2014; Hsu et al., 2015; van der Wal et al., 2002; Wilkinson et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a statement of the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Certain proteins, including MHC class I molecules and natural killer cell ligands, can be targeted by more than one viral factor.
source: However, it is not yet known which viral factors target these proteins, and certain proteins, including MHC class I molecules and natural killer cell ligands, can be targeted by more than one viral factor (Fielding et al., 2014; Hsu et al., 2015; van der Wal et al., 2002; Wilkinson et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations to prior work.

claim: 170 stable cell lines were generated from immortalised primary human fetal foreskin fibroblasts (HFFF-TERTs), each expressing a single, canonical HCMV ORF with a C-terminal V5 tag.
source: To build a global picture of all HCMV virus-host and virus-virus protein interactions, 170 stable cell lines were generated from immortalised primary human fetal foreskin fibroblasts (HFFF-TERTs), each expressing a single, canonical HCMV ORF with a C-terminal V5 tag to facilitate immunoprecipitation (IP).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental approach.

claim: ORFL147C was included as a bait on the basis of high expression relative to all other viral ORFs detected previously by proteomics.
source: Two non-canonical ORFs, ORFL147C and ORFS343C, were also included on the basis of either high or low expression respectively, relative to all other viral ORFs detected previously by proteomics (Figure 1 – Figure Supplement 1A, Supplementary file 1A) (Fielding et al., 2017; Weekes et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1 – Figure Supplement 1A.

claim: ORFS343C was included as a bait on the basis of low expression relative to all other viral ORFs detected previously by proteomics.
source: Two non-canonical ORFs, ORFL147C and ORFS343C, were also included on the basis of either high or low expression respectively, relative to all other viral ORFs detected previously by proteomics (Figure 1 – Figure Supplement 1A, Supplementary file 1A) (Fielding et al., 2017; Weekes et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1 – Figure Supplement 1A.

claim: Expression of each tagged viral 'bait' protein was validated by immunoblotting (IB), MS or RT-qPCR, apart from UL136 which could not be detected by any method.
source: Prior to profiling by IP-mass spectrometry (IP-MS), expression of each tagged viral 'bait' protein was validated by immunoblotting (IB), MS or RT-qPCR, apart from UL136 which could not be detected by any method (Figure 1 – Figure Supplement 1B, Supplementary file 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1 – Figure Supplement 1B.

claim: IP was performed in cells infected with Merlin strain HCMV at multiplicity of infection (MOI) of 2 for 60 hr.
source: To examine the full range of virus-virus interactions in addition to virus-host interactions, IP was performed in cells infected with Merlin strain HCMV at multiplicity of infection (MOI) of 2 for 60 hr.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental conditions.

claim: Merlin strain HCMV contains a full length genome and expresses all HCMV genes apart from UL128 and RL13.
source: Merlin contains a full length genome and expresses all HCMV genes apart from UL128 and RL13.
evidence: This is a statement about the properties of the viral strain used.

claim: For 153 baits with zero or one transmembrane (TM) region predicted by Uniprot, an NP40-based lysis buffer was used.
source: For 153 baits with zero or one transmembrane (TM) region predicted by Uniprot, an NP40-based lysis buffer was used; for 18 baits with >1 TM region, a digitonin-based buffer was used, as this has previously been demonstrated to improve identifications of interacting proteins ('prey') (Babu et al., 2012) (Supplementary file 1B).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental approach, supported by a citation.

claim: For 18 baits with >1 TM region, a digitonin-based buffer was used, as this has previously been demonstrated to improve identifications of interacting proteins.
source: For 153 baits with zero or one transmembrane (TM) region predicted by Uniprot, an NP40-based lysis buffer was used; for 18 baits with >1 TM region, a digitonin-based buffer was used, as this has previously been demonstrated to improve identifications of interacting proteins ('prey') (Babu et al., 2012) (Supplementary file 1B).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental approach, supported by a citation.

claim: Each dataset was scored separately using the CompPASS algorithm to better model detergent-specific variation in IP-MS background.
source: Each dataset was scored separately using the CompPASS algorithm (Huttlin et al., 2015; Sowa et al., 2009) to better model detergent-specific variation in IP-MS background.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the data analysis approach, supported by citations.

claim: Previous studies have estimated a 5% false discovery rate when employing a similar strategy with a top NWD score cutoff of 2%.
source: Previous studies have estimated a 5% false discovery rate when employing a similar strategy with a top NWD score cutoff of 2% (Sowa et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a statement supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: For HCMV UL120 and UL142, no interacting proteins passed the stringent filters employed.
source: For HCMV UL120 and UL142, no interacting proteins passed the stringent filters employed.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results.

claim: For seven viral proteins, only the bait itself passed filtering, leaving 162 viral baits with ≥1 HCIP.
source: For seven further proteins, only the bait itself passed filtering, leaving 162 viral baits with ≥1 HCIP.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results.

claim: In total, 3572 interactions were detected across all 162 baits.
source: In total, 3572 interactions were detected across all 162 baits, with a range of 1–174 interactions per bait, reflecting a scale-free degree distribution typical of protein interaction networks.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results.

claim: The range of interactions per bait was 1–174 interactions.
source: In total, 3572 interactions were detected across all 162 baits, with a range of 1–174 interactions per bait, reflecting a scale-free degree distribution typical of protein interaction networks.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results.

claim: The median number of interactions per bait was 9.
source: The median number of interactions per bait was 9, similar to previously observed in the Bioplex 2.0 human interactome (Huttlin et al., 2015) (Materials and methods; Supplementary file 2A, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the results, with comparison to prior work.

claim: The median number of interactions per bait was similar to previously observed in the Bioplex 2.0 human interactome.
source: The median number of interactions per bait was 9, similar to previously observed in the Bioplex 2.0 human interactome (Huttlin et al., 2015) (Materials and methods; Supplementary file 2A, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is a statement comparing the results to prior work, supported by a citation.

claim: Nucleosome remodeling (NuRD) complex components were significantly enriched among HCMV-interacting proteins.
source: Nucleosome remodeling (NuRD) complex components were significantly enriched among HCMV-interacting proteins.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by pathway analysis shown in Figure 2.

claim: The NuRD complex plays major roles in cellular chromatin remodeling.
source: The NuRD complex plays major roles in cellular chromatin remodeling, and is known to be co-opted by HCMV UL29 and UL38 to enhance expression of immediate-early genes (Savaryn et al., 2013; Terhune et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge, supported by citations.

claim: The NuRD complex is known to be co-opted by HCMV UL29 and UL38 to enhance expression of immediate-early genes.
source: The NuRD complex plays major roles in cellular chromatin remodeling, and is known to be co-opted by HCMV UL29 and UL38 to enhance expression of immediate-early genes (Savaryn et al., 2013; Terhune et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The interaction of UL29 and UL38 in a complex with all components of NuRD was confirmed.
source: The interaction of UL29 and UL38 in a complex with all components of NuRD was confirmed, in addition to p53 (Savaryn et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 2.

claim: UL29 interacted with multiple human proteins that function in histone deacetylation.
source: UL29 was also found to interact with multiple human proteins that function in histone deacetylation, which had not been observed previously (Figure 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 2.

claim: UL87, UL79, UL91 and UL95 are essential for viral replication and necessary for transcriptional activation of viral genes expressed with 'true late' kinetics.
source: UL87, UL79, UL91 and UL95 are essential for viral replication and necessary for transcriptional activation of viral genes expressed with 'true late' kinetics.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about these viral proteins.

claim: UL92 has a similar function to UL87, UL79, UL91 and UL95.
source: UL92 has a similar function, and it has been suggested that these five proteins may form one or more complexes that modulate RNA polymerase II activity (Isomura et al., 2011; Omoto and Mocarski, 2013; Omoto and Mocarski, 2014).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations to prior work.

claim: It has been suggested that UL87, UL79, UL91, UL95 and UL92 may form one or more complexes that modulate RNA polymerase II activity.
source: UL92 has a similar function, and it has been suggested that these five proteins may form one or more complexes that modulate RNA polymerase II activity (Isomura et al., 2011; Omoto and Mocarski, 2013; Omoto and Mocarski, 2014).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Interactome data confirmed that UL87 interacted with UL79, UL91 and UL95.
source: Interactome data confirmed that UL87 interacted with UL79, UL91 and UL95 but did not detect an interaction with UL92.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by interactome data.

claim: Interactome data did not detect an interaction between UL87 and UL92.
source: Interactome data confirmed that UL87 interacted with UL79, UL91 and UL95 but did not detect an interaction with UL92.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by interactome data.

claim: UL92 was one of the two least abundantly expressed viral proteins during HCMV infection.
source: This latter observation, and in fact the lack of identification of any viral-viral UL92 interactions, may be explained by our finding that UL92 was one of the two least abundantly expressed viral proteins during HCMV infection (Supplementary file 1A, bottom).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by IBAQ data in Supplementary file 1A.

claim: UL87 interacted with all 12 components of the RNA polymerase II (RPII) complex and the associated protein RPII Associated Protein 2 (RPAP2).
source: UL87 also interacted with all 12 components of the RNA polymerase II (RPII) complex and the associated protein RPII Associated Protein 2 (RPAP2) (Figure 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The UL87-RPII interaction was anticipated by analogy to the orthologous RPII-interacting Epstein-Barr virus protein BcRF1, but had not previously been demonstrated.
source: The UL87-RPII interaction was anticipated by analogy to the orthologous RPII-interacting Epstein-Barr virus protein BcRF1, but had not previously been demonstrated.
evidence: This is a statement comparing the results to prior knowledge about a related virus.

claim: Interaction of UL87, UL95 and UL79 with the UL97 protein kinase was novel.
source: Interaction of UL87, UL95 and UL79 with the UL97 protein kinase was also novel.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by interactome data.

claim: UL72 is a temporal protein profile 3 (Tp3)-class HCMV protein derived from deoxyuridine 5'-triphosphate nucleotidohydrolase (dUTPase) in other herpesviruses, but lacks dUTPase activity.
source: For example, UL72 is a temporal protein profile 3 (Tp3)-class HCMV protein derived from deoxyuridine 5'-triphosphate nucleotidohydrolase (dUTPase) in other herpesviruses, but lacks dUTPase activity (Caposio et al., 2004; McGeehan et al., 2001).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations to prior work.

claim: UL72 interacted with all 10 components of the CCR4-NOT (carbon catabolite repressor 4-negative on TATA) complex.
source: UL72 interacted with all 10 components of the CCR4-NOT (carbon catabolite repressor 4-negative on TATA) complex, which is a key regulator of gene expression from production of mRNAs in the nucleus to their degradation in the cytoplasm (Yi et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The CCR4-NOT complex is a key regulator of gene expression from production of mRNAs in the nucleus to their degradation in the cytoplasm.
source: UL72 interacted with all 10 components of the CCR4-NOT (carbon catabolite repressor 4-negative on TATA) complex, which is a key regulator of gene expression from production of mRNAs in the nucleus to their degradation in the cytoplasm (Yi et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge, supported by a citation.

claim: The interaction between UL72 and CNOT2/CNOT7 was confirmed by co-IP.
source: The interaction between UL72 and CNOT2/CNOT7 was confirmed by co-IP (Figure 3A–B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3A–B.

claim: The hitherto uncharacterised viral UL145 protein is known to recruit the Cullin 4 E3 ligase scaffold and associated adaptor proteins, and to degrade helicase-like transcription factor (HLTF).
source: The hitherto uncharacterised viral UL145 protein is known to recruit the Cullin 4 E3 ligase scaffold and associated adaptor proteins, and to degrade helicase-like transcription factor (HLTF) (Nightingale et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a statement supported by a citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: Interactome data suggested that all human proteins interacting with UL145 and the paralogous RL1 were part of the ubiquitin conjugation pathway.
source: Interactome data suggested that all human proteins interacting with UL145 and the paralogous RL1 were part of the ubiquitin conjugation pathway (Supplementary file 2, Supplementary file 4), and furthermore that RL1 interacted with Cullin 4 (CUL4, Figure 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 2 and supplementary files.

claim: RL1 interacted with Cullin 4 (CUL4).
source: Interactome data suggested that all human proteins interacting with UL145 and the paralogous RL1 were part of the ubiquitin conjugation pathway (Supplementary file 2, Supplementary file 4), and furthermore that RL1 interacted with Cullin 4 (CUL4, Figure 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The interaction between RL1 and CUL4A was validated by co-IP.
source: The interaction with CUL4A was validated by co-IP (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Multiple other HCMV proteins interacted with elements of the ubiquitin transfer or conjugation pathways.
source: Multiple other HCMV proteins additionally interacted with elements of the ubiquitin transfer or conjugation pathways, including the inhibitor of apoptosis UL36, which bound the Cullin one scaffold, E3 ligase UBR5, and F-box component FBOX3.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by interactome data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The inhibitor of apoptosis UL36 bound the Cullin one scaffold, E3 ligase UBR5, and F-box component FBOX3.
source: Multiple other HCMV proteins additionally interacted with elements of the ubiquitin transfer or conjugation pathways, including the inhibitor of apoptosis UL36, which bound the Cullin one scaffold, E3 ligase UBR5, and F-box component FBOX3.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by interactome data shown in Figure 2.

claim: DNA helicase/primase component UL102 interacted with E3 ligase RNF114 and E2 conjugating enzyme UBE2L6.
source: Similarly, DNA helicase/primase component UL102 interacted with E3 ligase RNF114 and E2 conjugating enzyme UBE2L6 (Figure 2 and Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The tegument protein UL71 has an essential function in the final steps of secondary envelopment leading to infectious viral particles.
source: The tegument protein UL71 has an essential function in the final steps of secondary envelopment leading to infectious viral particles, but is expressed with Tp3 kinetics, suggesting the possibility of a role earlier during infection (Dietz et al., 2018; Meissner et al., 2012; Weekes et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations to prior work.

claim: UL71 is expressed with Tp3 kinetics, suggesting the possibility of a role earlier during infection.
source: The tegument protein UL71 has an essential function in the final steps of secondary envelopment leading to infectious viral particles, but is expressed with Tp3 kinetics, suggesting the possibility of a role earlier during infection (Dietz et al., 2018; Meissner et al., 2012; Weekes et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations to prior work and involves inference about potential function.

claim: UL71 interacted with multiple interferon-stimulated proteins.
source: UL71 interacted with multiple interferon-stimulated proteins (Figure 3D), including TRIM22, which restricts replication of HIV-1, influenza A and hepatitis B and C viruses (Lian and Sun, 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: TRIM22 restricts replication of HIV-1, influenza A and hepatitis B and C viruses.
source: UL71 interacted with multiple interferon-stimulated proteins (Figure 3D), including TRIM22, which restricts replication of HIV-1, influenza A and hepatitis B and C viruses (Lian and Sun, 2017).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge, supported by a citation.

claim: The UL71-TRIM22 interaction was validated by co-IP.
source: The UL71-TRIM22 interaction was validated by co-IP, suggesting that investigation of a putative innate immune role for UL71 will be important (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The US28 G-protein coupled receptor (GPCR) functions in both lytic and latent HCMV infection via constitutive signaling to activate distinct intracellular pathways.
source: The US28 G-protein coupled receptor (GPCR) functions in both lytic and latent HCMV infection via constitutive signaling to activate distinct intracellular pathways (Krishna et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a statement supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: US28 interacted with all quantified members of thick filament/muscle myosin complexes.
source: Here, US28 interacted with all quantified members of thick filament/muscle myosin complexes, namely myosin heavy and light chain components, a myosin binding protein and titin.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: US28 interaction with thick filament/muscle myosin complexes suggests an unanticipated role for US28 in processes such as regulation of the actin cytoskeleton or cytoskeletal remodeling.
source: This suggests an unanticipated role for US28 in processes such as regulation of the actin cytoskeleton or cytoskeletal remodeling (Wang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is an inference based on the interaction data, supported by a citation.

claim: The US27 GPCR interacted with multiple components of the SNARE complex.
source: For example, the US27 GPCR interacted with multiple components of the SNARE complex, whose primary function is to mediate vesicle fusion (Han et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The primary function of the SNARE complex is to mediate vesicle fusion.
source: For example, the US27 GPCR interacted with multiple components of the SNARE complex, whose primary function is to mediate vesicle fusion (Han et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge, supported by a citation.

claim: Envelope glycoprotein UL132 interacted with the AP-2 adaptor complex, which functions in clathrin-mediated endocytosis.
source: Envelope glycoprotein UL132 interacted with the AP-2 adaptor complex, which functions in clathrin-mediated endocytosis (Figure 2—figure supplement 1) (Collins et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and a citation.

claim: Tp1 and Tp2 protein HCIPs were enriched in NuRD complex members, proteins involved in histone deacetylation and proteins with SANT domains.
source: For example, Tp1 and Tp2 protein HCIPs were enriched in NuRD complex members, proteins involved in histone deacetylation and proteins with SANT domains (which function in chromatin remodelling).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Tp3 HCIPs were enriched in functions required for viral genomic replication and immune evasion.
source: Tp3 HCIPs were enriched in functions required for viral genomic replication and immune evasion, whilst Tp5 HCIPs were directed at intracellular trafficking and secretion (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Tp5 HCIPs were directed at intracellular trafficking and secretion.
source: Tp3 HCIPs were enriched in functions required for viral genomic replication and immune evasion, whilst Tp5 HCIPs were directed at intracellular trafficking and secretion (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Domain association analysis correctly predicted that HCMV glycoprotein UL141 interacts with TNFR cysteine-rich domains (TNFR c6).
source: This correctly predicted that HCMV glycoprotein UL141 interacts with TNFR cysteine-rich domains (TNFR c6), which has been demonstrated for TNFRSF10B and predicted for TNFRSF10A (Nemčovičová et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: UL141 also interacted with TNFRSF10D as reported.
source: UL141 also interacted with TNFRSF10D as reported (Smith et al., 2013) and was found to interact with TNFRSF1A, suggesting that these interactions may also occur via the TNFR c6 domain (Figure 4A, Supplementary file 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by a citation and data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: UL141 was found to interact with TNFRSF1A, suggesting that these interactions may also occur via the TNFR c6 domain.
source: UL141 also interacted with TNFRSF10D as reported (Smith et al., 2013) and was found to interact with TNFRSF1A, suggesting that these interactions may also occur via the TNFR c6 domain (Figure 4A, Supplementary file 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 4A, with inference about the domain involved.

claim: Domain analysis predicted that certain Herpes pp85 proteins interact with host SH3 domains.
source: Domain analysis predicted that certain Herpes pp85 proteins interact with host SH3 domains.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The viral tegument pp85 phosphoprotein UL25 interacted with SH3 domain-containing proteins NCK1 and NCK2.
source: Underlying interactome data suggested that the viral tegument pp85 phosphoprotein UL25 interacted with SH3 domain-containing proteins NCK1 (Non-catalytic region of protein tyrosine kinase 1) and NCK2.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by interactome data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: UL26 interacted with NCK2 but not NCK1.
source: Additionally, UL25 interacted with two other human proteins and the viral tegument protein UL26. UL26 had more diverse targets, including NCK2 but not NCK1 (Figure 4A–B, Supplementary file 2, Supplementary file 5).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 4A–B.

claim: UL25 has a proline-rich C-terminus.
source: UL25 has a proline-rich C-terminus, and NCK1 has three N-terminal SH3 regions.
